_comment: A planted-alert SIEM fixture for the S24 acceptance tests (REQ-VALID-002).
It models what a defender's pipeline reports after a coordinated purple-team window:
one alert per detection it *did* raise, quoted with the run nonce the payload carried,
plus the noise a real SIEM always has.
The planted set is deliberately partial, because a fixture where everything is seen
* T1190 linked to the run (initial access seen);
* T1059 linked to the run (execution seen);
* T1190 again, out of the window (the defender was not watching yet);
* T1486 (impact) with no nonce — the SIEM fired, but not for our test;
* a defensive-telemetry alert naming no ATT&CK technique at all.
The unseen technique this fixture is designed to demonstrate is T1565.001
(m3.state-marker, stored data manipulation): the lab SIEM has no rule for it, so it
comes back as a coverage gap AND as the deliberate Sigma rule-miss.
Placeholders ({{NONCE}}) are substituted by the test with the run's generated nonce,
because the nonce is minted per run and must not be a constant in a committed file.
No credential appears anywhere in this fixture.

alerts.title: SQL injection attempt against web parameter
alerts.message: SQL metacharacter sequence in request parameter (test nonce={{NONCE}})

alerts.title: Web worker spawned a shell
alerts.description: php-fpm spawned /bin/sh; the payload carried nonce={{NONCE}}

alerts.title: SQL injection attempt against web parameter
alerts.message: before the coordinated window opened; test nonce={{NONCE}}

alerts.title: Mass file encryption behaviour
alerts.message: unrelated estate traffic; no test nonce on this one

alerts.title: EDR sensor health degraded
alerts.message: no ATT&CK technique is named for a health alert, so it scores nothing
